_note: Places that were N/A for surfing but have a real surf scene within a day trip (web check, 11 Oct 2026). To be sent to Gemini; it decides applicability.

places.amsterdam: Wijk aan Zee is about 30 minutes away and has surf schools and rentals; Zandvoort, 30 minutes away, also has schools. North Sea beach breaks, season about March to October.
places.andalucia: The Atlantic coast of Cádiz (El Palmar, Los Caños de Meca, Conil) has year-round surf schools and camps, and Tarifa is a winter base. Best in autumn, winter and spring.
places.bordeaux: Lacanau is about an hour away: sandbank beach breaks, several surf schools, and a Bordeaux surf school that runs day trips.
places.borneo: Sabah has a young but real scene: Kudat and Tanjung Simpang Mengayau (waves to about 6 ft, best December to March) and Karambunai near Kota Kinabalu, which has hosted the Borneo Surf Festival and lessons.
places.edinburgh: Belhaven Bay at Dunbar (a surf school since 2004, about an hour away) and Pease Bay (Momentum Surf School) in East Lothian. Cold North Sea, best September to February.
places.hokkaido: Surf exists on both coasts, mostly empty and very cold (drysuit in winter). Sources are thin on named spots and schools, so this one is a judgment call for Gemini.
places.istanbul: Kilyos is about an hour and 15 minutes away on the Black Sea with surf schools; Kerpe, about an hour away, has a surf academy. Short summer season and winter swell.
places.quebec-city: Montreal has a river-wave scene on the St. Lawrence (Habitat 67 and Big Joe) with schools (KSF, Imagine Surfboards), May to October.
places.rome: Ostia and Fregene have several surf schools (some since 2005 and 2006), but waves are small and come mostly ahead of southern storms. A judgment call for Gemini.
places.seoul: Yangyang (Jukdo and Ingu beaches) is about two hours away with over 100 surf businesses and year-round schools; Korea's main surf scene.
places.snowdonia: Wales has a real coastal scene: Llangennith and Rhossili on the Gower, and Freshwater West in Pembrokeshire, with schools. Biggest in winter.
places.southeast-alaska: Yakutat is Alaska's best-known surf town (daily jet service and ferry stops; best mid-April to mid-June and August to September) and Sitka's Sandy Beach is reachable by road in winter.
places.tokyo-kyoto: Shonan is under an hour and a half from Tokyo and Chiba (Ichinomiya, an Olympic surf venue) about 1.5 hours away, with over 20 surf shops along its beach road. Best August to October.
places.tuscany: Versilia (Viareggio, Cinquale) is called the surfing capital of Italy, with a Livorno scene and schools near San Vincenzo and Punta Ala. Best in autumn and winter storms.
places.upper-peninsula: Lake Superior surfing around Marquette (Presque Isle, Grand Marais), in fall and winter storms until the ice. There is no surf shop in Marquette, so this is a judgment call for Gemini.
places.falklands: Marginal, sent anyway at the owner's request. Surf Bay near Stanley is a fickle beach break that works only a few times a year in very cold water, with no schools or rentals found.
places.chiapas: Marginal, sent anyway at the owner's request. Pacific sandbars such as Puerto Arista have uncrowded waves for all levels, but no surf schools or camps turned up and the coast is a long way from the places visitors go.
places.napa: Marginal, sent anyway at the owner's request. Inland wine country; the Sonoma coast has a consistent cold beach break (Salmon Creek) with regular great white shark sightings, and no surf schools turned up.
